title: Bharata refuses the crown
hook: the son a mother schemed for refuses the crown, and has to convince Rama's mother he never wanted it
tomorrow: why does Bharata come with an army?

segments.voice: Yesterday: your line, an elder brother stands as a father. Bharata came home, asked first for Rama, and Kaikeyi told him the throne was his.
screen: `AN ELDER BROTHER STANDS AS A FATHER.`

segments.voice: Kaikeyi has been waiting for this conversation: her son home, the crown ready. What she gets is fury. Bharata doesn't thank her. He tells her she has destroyed the family, killed his father with grief, and sent away the brother he loves. The kingdom she won for him, he says, he will never accept. Then he walks out, to face the person he dreads most: Kausalya, Rama's mother.
screen: `NO THANKS, ONLY GRIEF.` → `I WILL NEVER ACCEPT IT.` → `NOW, KAUSALYA.`

segments.voice: Kausalya has every reason to suspect him. Here is the son who gains everything from her son's exile. She says so, bitterly: you wanted the kingdom, now you have it. Bharata falls at her feet and swears. Valmiki gives him a long chain of oaths, each naming a wrong he'd rather be guilty of than this. May I carry the guilt of one who betrays a trust, who strikes a sleeping person, who turns away a guest, if I ever wanted Rama gone. Kausalya believes him. She takes his head in her lap, and they weep together. Then the duty that can't wait. Under Vasishtha's guidance, Bharata performs his father's funeral rites, and the family offers water at the Sarayu. That offering, tarpana, water poured from the hands for those who have died, is still part of how Hindu families remember their dead. Afterward Shatrughna catches Manthara, the maid who started it all. Bharata stops him: Rama would never forgive us. Here's why Hindus honor Bharata so deeply. A crown was handed to him, the biggest prize there is. But it was won by wronging his brother, and by custom and by dharma the throne belonged to the eldest, Rama. What comes through adharma, through wrong, isn't worth holding. Bharata's refusal is why the tradition remembers him as the model brother. And so the week closes: a hill, a confession, a curse, a boy who became Shravan Kumar, and a son who put dharma before the crown.
screen: `KAUSALYA'S SUSPICION.` · `A CHAIN OF OATHS.` · `TARPANA: WATER FOR THE DEAD.` · `THE THRONE WAS RAMA'S BY DHARMA.` · then, large: `DHARMA BEFORE THE CROWN.`

segments.voice: Many Hindu families remember those who have died by offering water from cupped hands, as Bharata did at the Sarayu. If you'd like, hold a little water in your palms, think of someone who has died, and let it pour slowly into a bowl or a plant. If you don't pray, simply hold a glass of water, say their name, and let one long breath go with it.
Bharata's journey. He refuses his mother's gift, swears his innocence to Kausalya, performs his father's last rites, and puts dharma before the crown.
Your line: dharma before the crown. Bharata refused the prize, and Rama's mother believed him. That's day five hundred forty-six.
